findings.title: amountCents contract silently wrong for currencies whose minor unit is not 1/100 (JPY, KWD, BHD)
findings.evidence: The function accepts any ISO 4217 code but always divides by 100: 'return formatter.format(amountCents / 100);'. Intl.NumberFormat derives default fraction digits from the currency, so a 0-digit currency and a 3-digit currency both get a 2-decimal amount.
findings.recommendation: Either reject currencies whose resolved minor-unit count is not 2 (e.g. use Intl.NumberFormat(locale,{style:'currency',currency}).resolvedOptions().maximumFractionDigits and throw if !== 2), or scale by 10 ** digits and document that amountCents means minor units rather than always 1/100.

findings.title: Safe-integer range exceeds double cent precision, so very large amounts can display one cent off
findings.evidence: The guard accepts up to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER: 'if (!Number.isSafeInteger(amountCents)) {', but amountCents/100 for magnitudes around 2^46 and above lands on doubles spaced ~0.015625 apart, which is coarser than 0.01, so the rounded 2-digit display can be wrong by a cent (e.g. a cents value whose true fractional part is .93 near 9e13 renders as .94).
findings.recommendation: Lower the accepted bound (e.g. require |amountCents| <= 2**45) or format via an integer/string split (whole = Math.trunc(amountCents/100), frac = abs(amountCents)%100) and pass an exact decimal string rather than a double.

findings.title: Intl.NumberFormat constructed on every call
findings.evidence: A new formatter is allocated per invocation: 'const formatter = new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, {' — Intl construction is expensive relative to format(), so any table/loop or render path calling formatMoney repeatedly pays that cost per row.
findings.recommendation: Memoize formatters in a module-level Map keyed by locale plus currency, and reuse the cached instance; keep the throw-on-invalid-currency behaviour by letting the first construction fail.

findings.title: No tests accompany the new module
findings.evidence: The diff adds only the implementation and a convenience wrapper, 'export function formatUsd(cents) {', with no test file covering negative amounts, non-integer rejection, unsupported/invalid currency RangeError, or locale overrides.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests asserting the TypeError path for non-integers/NaN/Infinity, a negative amount, an explicit locale override, and at least one non-default currency.
